// diagnostic

E2910

`reactive.{kind}` needs a lambda, not {type}.

What

`reactive.{kind}` needs a lambda, not {type}.

Why

`reactive.derived`/`reactive.effect` build a reactive value from a `() -> …` body so it can re-run when a signal changes (D-REACT1=B). A non-lambda argument has nothing to re-run.

Fix

Write `reactive.derived(() -> … )` or `reactive.effect(() -> { … })`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E2910: tests/ui/reactive_derived_not_lambda.stderr.

Error [E2910]: `reactive.derived` needs a lambda, not Int (a whole number)
  --> tests/ui/reactive_derived_not_lambda.jet:4:27
    |
  4 |     d := reactive.derived(42)
    |                           ^^
 Why: a reactive derived is built from a `() => …` body so it can re-run when a signal changes
 Fix: write `reactive.derived(() => { … })`
